stories.title: Man, 30s, arrested in Waterford death investigation
stories.summary: A man in his 30s has been arrested as part of the investigation into the death of a woman in Co Waterford. The body of the woman, who is believed to be aged in her 80s, was discovered at a house in a rural area at Ardsallagh near Youghal Bridge yesterday afternoon. Her body has been removed to University Hospital Waterford, where a post-mortem examination will be carried out. Gardaí said the results of the post-mortem determine the course of their investigations.

stories.title: Trump says Iran deal going to a 'second stage'
stories.summary: US President Donald ⁠Trump has said that the Iran deal was going to a second stage, and ‌that ⁠the US would not be investing any money in Iran. "We have our deal ‌done with Iran, and it ⁠should be successful, ‌it goes to a second ⁠stage, ‌which I think would be actually easier," he said during a press briefing at the G7 summit in France. He said that under the deal Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and warned that "all hell" would break out if it tried to acquire one. Earlier, Iran's foreign minister said Iran and the US will start a new round of negotiations on Friday in Switzerland to reach a final peace agreement after the official start of an interim agreement.

stories.title: Councillors 'disappointed' by Harris dereliction remarks
stories.summary: A national body representing county and city councillors has expressed disappointment at comments by Tánaiste Simon Harris that local authorities have not done enough to tackle dereliction. Mr Harris is to update the Cabinet in his role as Minister for Finance on plans to introduce a new Derelict Property Tax in 107 cities and towns across the State. Speaking on Sunday, the Fine Gael leader said he was angry and frustrated that local authorities had "not done enough" to tackle abandoned buildings by chasing derelict site levies and said he would take some powers away from them. "The association is disappointed by comments suggesting that local authorities have 'badly failed' in administering the Derelict Sites Levy," the statement said.

stories.title: Trust in major brands but news avoidance grows - report
stories.summary: The annual Digital News Report for Ireland 2026 shows that Irish people continue to trust major news brands, but are losing trust in news more generally. Down eight percentage points from last year, 42% of the adult population surveyed said that they trust most news "most of the time" which is a sharp decrease from 50% answering that same question last year. The figures are included in the 12th edition of the annual report published in Cork today by Coimisiún na Meán. The report, by the Reuters Institute at Oxford University, is the largest ongoing comparative study of news consumption in the world.

stories.title: Eight dead in B-52 bomber crash in California
stories.summary: Eight people died when a US B-52 bomber crashed and erupted into a catastrophic fire shortly after takeoff at an air force base in California, officials said. The heavy bomber was on a routine testing mission with a mixture of military, government and civilian contractors on board when it came down at Edwards Air Force Base, 95km north of Los Angeles. Footage of the aftermath of the crash, which officials said was "unsurvivable," showed a large charred patch of ground on which almost nothing remained of the huge plane manufactured by Boeing. "Edwards Air Force Base experienced a horrible tragedy, and we lost eight great Americans," Colonel James Hayes told reporters at the base.

stories.title: Celebrations taking place across Dublin for Bloomsday
stories.summary: Celebrations will take place across Dublin to mark Bloomsday, the day immortalised by James Joyce in his novel Ulysses. For more than 70 years, 16 June has been marked throughout the capital with recitals and re-enactments from scenes from the author's most famous work. Set across a single day in Dublin in 1904, Ulysses continues to captivate readers and writers around the world. James Joyce famously said that he wanted to "give a picture of Dublin so complete that if the city one day suddenly disappeared from the earth, it could be reconstructed out of my book".
